name: Stinoment Growth Assistant
author: STINOMENT

sections.description:
Is your site slow, hard to find on Google, or not safe? Most owners find out too late, when the visitors are already gone.

Growth Assistant checks your whole site every day. Then it tells you, in plain words, what is wrong, where it is, why it matters and how to fix it. Many problems have a fix button. Nothing changes until you click it, and you can undo every change.

The plugin is free. You do not need an account or a subscription. It is made by STINOMENT, a team that has helped hundreds of websites grow. We use it every day on our own sites and on our clients’ sites.

1. A daily check-up with more than 50 checks

Security, site health, SEO, content, links, speed, WooCommerce and comments. Every finding comes with clear next steps. Each day you also see the three tasks that help your site the most.

2. Google and Bing numbers you can understand

Connect Google Search Console (four easy ways) and Bing. You see clicks, views and position for up to 16 months. The plugin also tells you which pages are close to page one, which pages are losing visitors, and why Google has a problem with your sitemap.

3. Image tools: alt text, smaller files and WebP

  • Writes alt text for all your images in one click. The text comes from the page where the image is used, so Google understands your pictures.
  • Makes big images much lighter. You see a real before and after sample first.
  • Changes JPG and PNG images to WebP, the modern format. Your old files are kept, so you can undo at any time.

4. Security that does not get in your way

  • Login protection, a private login address and two-step login.
  • File health: your files are compared with the real files from WordPress.org.
  • Alerts by email, Telegram or webhook when the site goes down or a file changes.
  • An activity log of logins and important changes.

5. Backups

A content backup or a full backup of all files, made in small steps so it works on shared hosting. You choose how many days to keep them.

6. Speed test

Test any page on phone or computer. You get a grade from A to F, the problems in plain words, a fix for each one, and the plugin or theme that makes the page heavy.

7. Tools to grow

  • A 27-day growth plan built from your own check-up, week by week.
  • A content coach that finds your weak posts and products each day and shows what is missing.
  • Site strength and trust scores, month by month.
  • Competitor watch, store money leaks for WooCommerce, push notifications and a monthly report.

8. A toolbox for everyday work

Redirects for missing pages, safe editing of robots.txt, llms.txt and .htaccess, email delivery (SMTP), a cookie banner that really waits for consent, protection switches and more.

9. An AI assistant that does the work for you

Tell the AI what you want, in your own words: “find the posts about fake pages and change their titles”, “move Russian spam comments with links to spam”, “write descriptions for my top tags”, “change the copyright text in my footer”, “change this Elementor button”, “are my settings standard?”. It reads your site, then shows a card with every change. Nothing changes until you press “Do it”, and every change can be undone. It also manages plugin and theme settings, CSS and the cache, and reads competitors’ posts. It never runs code (code it writes is only shown to copy), never touches users or passwords, and never deletes anything for ever. Give it your own rules once (text or a file), and it keeps a memory of your site, so every answer fits your business. Free sites get one AI question every 24 hours.

Want more help from AI?

Premium gives you more AI each day, plus social posts, article ideas and full drafts written with your own answers, and a refresh for old posts. All checks and tools above stay free for everyone.

Built for everyday hosting

Work runs in short steps or small background jobs, never while visitors open your pages. English and Persian, with “?” notes on every screen.

Works with AI assistants

On WordPress 6.9+, the report, fixes, undo and Toolbox tools are in the Abilities API for MCP assistants (administrators only).

About STINOMENT

STINOMENT is an IT team that builds, fixes and grows websites, and can do the SEO and speed work for you.

  • English website, guides and plugin news: https://stinoment.com/
  • Persian website (فارسی): https://stinoment.com/fa/

External services

This plugin can connect to these services. Nothing personal is sent.

  • IndexNow (api.indexnow.org) – only when you turn on the IndexNow switch. When a post is published or updated, its address, your site host name and your IndexNow key are sent, so search engines that use IndexNow (Bing, Yandex and others) learn about the change. Documentation: https://www.indexnow.org/documentation · Microsoft privacy statement: https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement · Yandex legal documents: https://yandex.com/legal/
  • WordPress.org Plugins API (api.wordpress.org) – during a check-up, the folder names of your active plugins are sent to learn when each plugin was last updated. Privacy policy: https://wordpress.org/about/privacy/
  • WordPress.org files (api.wordpress.org, downloads.wordpress.org, core.svn.wordpress.org) – only when you use File health: your WordPress version and locale, and the folder name and version of each plugin, are sent to download the original file fingerprints; to repair a WordPress file, that original file is downloaded. Privacy policy: https://wordpress.org/about/privacy/
  • Google Search Console API (searchconsole.googleapis.com, oauth2.googleapis.com) – only with the “own key” Search Console method: your site’s property address and the date ranges are sent with your own service account, to read your search numbers. When you press “Add to Search Console” or “Remove from Search Console” on the Search tab, the sitemap address is also sent, to add it to or remove it from your property. Terms: https://developers.google.com/terms · Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • STINOMENT server (api.stinoment.com) – only with the “STINOMENT email” or “Sign in with Google” methods: your site address and a random check token are sent once to register the site, then the property and date ranges of each Search Console request. The server reads Google’s numbers for you and returns them; it does not keep them. Privacy policy: https://stinoment.com/privacy-policy/
  • STINOMENT contact form (api.stinoment.com) – only when you fill in the form on the “About us” screen, tick the agreement box and press “Send message”: your name, email, phone (if given), website address, the service you chose and your message are sent so the STINOMENT team can answer you. Nothing is sent before that. Privacy policy: https://stinoment.com/privacy-policy/
  • STINOMENT Web Report (api.stinoment.com) – off by default; only if you turn on “Share anonymous monthly totals” in Growth → STINOMENT Web Report. Once a month, anonymous totals of the month before are sent (search, health, speed and security numbers, no visitor data, no user names, no passwords). You can read the exact summary before you agree, and turning it off deletes everything your site shared. The full list is in the FAQ: “What does the STINOMENT Web Report send?”. Privacy policy: https://stinoment.com/privacy-policy/
  • Browser push services – only if you turn on Push notifications and press “Send”, or an admin turns on “Browser alerts” in the “Keep me posted” box (then only when something urgent happens on the site). For each follower the site sends an empty, signed request to the push address their own browser gave (Google Firebase Cloud Messaging for Chrome, Edge on Android and Opera; Mozilla for Firefox; Microsoft for Edge on Windows; Apple for Safari). The message text is not sent to them: the visitor’s browser then reads it from your own site. The push addresses are kept only in your database and are deleted with the plugin. Google: https://firebase.google.com/terms · https://policies.google.com/privacy · Mozilla: https://www.mozilla.org/about/legal/terms/services/ · https://www.mozilla.org/privacy/ · Microsoft: https://www.microsoft.com/servicesagreement · https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement · Apple: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/terms/site.html · https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/
  • STINOMENT bot (api.stinoment.com, with Telegram api.telegram.org or Bale tapi.bale.ai) – only after you press “Connect” in Security → Alerts and press Start in the bot. Your site address and name, the alert text and a short weekly report are sent, and the server checks about every 5 minutes that your site is up. Full list in the FAQ: “What does the STINOMENT bot send?”. Privacy policy: https://stinoment.com/privacy-policy/ · Telegram: https://telegram.org/tos · https://telegram.org/privacy · Bale: https://bale.ai/
  • Speed test (api.stinoment.com, with Google PageSpeed Insights and Chrome UX Report) – only when you press “Test on phone” or “Test on computer” in Growth → Speed test, and then once a week if you keep the weekly test on. The address of the page you test (a page of your own site), the device and your language are sent to the STINOMENT server, which asks Google’s PageSpeed Insights to open the page and sends back the scores, the problems and small screenshots. Pressing “Show the 6 months” sends your site address to read Google’s public real-visitor numbers (Chrome UX Report). No visitor data is sent. Privacy policy: https://stinoment.com/privacy-policy/ · Google terms: https://developers.google.com/terms · Google privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • Site strength (api.stinoment.com, with Open PageRank by DomCop) – only after you press “Check domain strength” in Growth → Site strength and trust, then once a month. Only your domain name is sent; the STINOMENT server asks Open PageRank for its public score and rank. The trust score is worked out on your own site and nothing is sent for it. Privacy policy: https://stinoment.com/privacy-policy/ · Open PageRank service and terms: https://www.domcop.com/openpagerank/
  • Google Site Kit – with the Site Kit method, data is read from the Site Kit plugin inside your own site; Site Kit talks to Google under its own terms.
  • Bing Webmaster Tools API (ssl.bing.com) – only after you add a Bing API key: your site address and key are sent to read your Bing numbers, and the addresses of your most linked pages to read who links to them. Microsoft privacy statement: https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement
  • Telegram Bot API (api.telegram.org) and Bale Bot API (tapi.bale.ai) – only if you add a bot token: the alert text (site name, what happened, your site address) is sent to the chat you choose. Telegram terms: https://telegram.org/tos · privacy: https://telegram.org/privacy · Bale: https://bale.ai/
  • Your own webhook (Slack, Discord, Google Chat, Teams) – only if you add one: the same alert text is sent to that address.
  • IRNIC WHOIS (whois.nic.ir, port 43) – only for sites on a .ir domain, because .ir domains are not in RDAP. Once a week the site’s domain name is sent to read when the registration ends. Nothing else is sent. Service by IRNIC, the .ir registry. Terms and privacy: https://www.nic.ir/
  • STINOMENT Premium (api.stinoment.com) – only when you open the Premium screen. Sent: your site address, the admin’s IP address and the site language, to show the price and check that the AI is offered in your region (the IP is stored only when refused). When you buy: the email you type and the transaction ID you paste. “Start my free days” sends the same details, and the server checks the bot link (and the Web Report when asked). Payment goes from your own wallet to STINOMENT; the plugin never sees wallet keys. Terms: https://stinoment.com/terms/ Privacy: https://stinoment.com/privacy-policy/
  • STINOMENT AI assistant (api.stinoment.com, with Anthropic’s Claude API) – when you open the Assistant screen, write a message or press an AI task button. Sent: your message, the chat, a short site summary, and the parts of your site the AI reads for your job (full list in the FAQ: “What does the AI assistant send?”). The server passes them to Anthropic and keeps only the cost and time, not the text. Privacy: https://stinoment.com/privacy-policy/ · Anthropic: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy
  • STINOMENT problem report (api.stinoment.com) – only when you fill in “Report a problem” and press Send: your text, your email (if given), your site address and the WordPress, PHP and plugin versions are sent so the STINOMENT team can fix it.
  • RDAP service (rdap.org) – only if you turn on the domain expiry alert. Once a week your site’s domain name (for example example.com) is sent to read when the domain registration ends. Nothing else is sent. Service by the RDAP.org project, which forwards the request to the registry of your domain: https://about.rdap.org/ · Privacy information: https://about.rdap.org/#privacy
  • STINOMENT brand check (api.stinoment.com, with Anthropic’s Claude API and web search) – only when you press “Ask the AI” in Growth → Your brand in AI answers. Sent: your brand name, site address and screen language. The server keeps only the cost, time and date of your last check; the answer is kept on your site. Privacy: https://stinoment.com/privacy-policy/ · Anthropic: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy
  • STINOMENT link data (api.stinoment.com) – only when you open Growth → Link opportunities. Domain names only are sent: your own domain and the competitor domains on that screen. The server answers from the open Common Crawl web graph (https://commoncrawl.org/terms-of-use) and deletes its own copy of the answers after about 10 days; your answers are kept on your site. Privacy policy: https://stinoment.com/privacy-policy/
  • Competitor sites and pages you ask about – Competitor watch opens the sites you add at most once a day (home page, sitemap, feed). In the AI assistant, when you ask, it opens the feed or public WordPress API of competitors you name, or a public page you name, like a visitor; the text goes to the AI to answer you.
  • Websites you link to (link checker) – during the broken links check, the plugin opens the addresses that appear in your own posts, with a plain request that sends no personal data, to see if the page still exists. Each site is a different service under its own terms.
  • YouTube thumbnails (i.ytimg.com) – only if you turn on the lightweight video embeds switch. Visitors’ browsers load the video’s preview picture from YouTube, and YouTube’s player loads only after a click. Terms: https://www.youtube.com/t/terms · Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Included libraries

  • QR Code Generator for JavaScript by Kazuhiko Arase, MIT license (assets/js/vendor/qrcode.js), used to show the two-step login QR code.
  • Fonts under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 (assets/fonts, license files next to them): Vazirmatn by Saber Rastikerdar, Lalezar by Borna Izadpanah, Inter by Rasmus Andersson. Used in the admin screens and the cookie banner, loaded from your own site.

sections.installation:
1. In your dashboard go to Plugins → Add New, search for “Stinoment Growth Assistant” and click Install, or upload the ZIP file.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Open Growth Assistant in the admin menu and click “Run check-up”. The first check-up takes about a minute.
  4. Optional: connect Search Console from the Search Console tab.
sections.faq:
What exactly does it do?

Search Console, explained

The plugin reads your numbers from Google and Bing once a day, so it adds no tracking and no load to your visitors.

  • Clicks, impressions, click rate and average position for 7 days up to 16 months (all Google keeps), with a chart and a comparison with the period before.
  • A plain-language analysis of strengths and weaknesses: pages close to page one, searches that see you but do not click, pages losing traffic, two pages competing for the same search, mobile versus desktop and more.
  • Devices, countries, top pages and searches, Google Images, Video, News and Discover, special result types (stars, prices, FAQ), and a “Is this page in Google?” check.
  • Sitemap warnings explained: Google only gives a number, so the plugin reads the sitemap like Google and finds the cause (redirects, missing pages, noindex, other domains, wrong dates).
  • Links from other sites (from Bing, as Google’s API has none): most linked pages, linking sites, link words, spam links, and lost links to pages that are gone, with a redirect in one click.
  • A “Google (28 days)” column in your posts, pages and products lists.
  • Four ways to connect Google (Site Kit, a read-only service email, your own service account key, or Google sign-in) and one for Bing (API key).

Daily check-up

More than 50 checks in nine areas, explained without jargon:

  • Security: backups, common weak spots, security headers the browser really gets, easy-to-guess admin names, exposed files, plugins that are no longer maintained.
  • Site health: WordPress, PHP and plugin updates, overlapping plugins, HTTPS, public debug logs, scheduled tasks.
  • SEO: titles, meta descriptions, duplicate titles, image alt text, robots.txt, sitemaps, long URLs, several SEO plugins at once, phone-friendly layout (viewport, zoom, responsive theme, too-wide tables and videos), structured data (broken schema code, missing fields Google needs, product, article and breadcrumb data), and icon links or buttons without a name.
  • Content: thin posts, posts with the same text, missing featured images, extra H1 headings, categories without descriptions, one-off tags, outdated posts, and missing trust pages (privacy policy, terms, contact, about, returns for shops).
  • Links: pages without internal links, broken links, unsafe links.
  • Speed: page cache, heavy images, settings loaded on every page, database clean-up.
  • Your pages as Google sees them: the real HTML of your home, blog and shop pages.
  • WooCommerce: products without price, image or description, and missing shop pages.
  • Comments: spam waiting in the queue and visitors still waiting for an answer.

Anything that is a choice on your site (products without a price, posts without a featured image) can be turned off with “Don’t remind me”, and turned on again in Settings.

Some fixes are applied for you after you agree, in small groups you can review one by one: alt text for images, H1 headings changed to H2 (also in Elementor pages), first descriptions for categories, redirects for broken internal links.

Toolbox

  • Backups: a content backup (database) or a full backup of all files and the database, built in small steps so it works on shared hosting. Old backups are removed after the number of days you choose.
  • Images: WebP conversion and smaller copies of very large photos.
  • Redirects and missing pages: see which missing addresses real visitors open, with a suggested target for each. Your home page, dashboard and login addresses are protected and never offered for redirection.
  • Important files: robots.txt, llms.txt and .htaccess with safe suggestions. Every .htaccess change is tested at once and rolled back if the site stops responding.
  • Protection and speed switches: XML-RPC, user name hiding, file editor, security headers, Heartbeat, Gravatar, IndexNow and more.
  • Email delivery: SMTP with ready settings for common providers, a test button, a log and the SPF and DMARC records your domain needs.
  • Cookie consent: finds the trackers your site really uses, writes the banner and the privacy text from them, makes Google tags wait (Consent Mode v2) and holds other trackers back until the visitor says yes. Persian and English, with Vazirmatn, Lalezar or Inter fonts.
  • Also: social profiles in structured data, a comment spam guard without captcha, and video compression in your browser.

Security

  • Login protection that pauses addresses, never user names, so nobody can lock you out on purpose.
  • A private login address, with a wp-config.php switch in case you forget it.
  • Two-step login with authenticator apps and backup codes.
  • File health: compares WordPress and plugin files with the originals from WordPress.org and repairs changed core files.
  • Alerts by email, Telegram or webhook (Slack, Discord, Google Chat, Teams) when the site goes down, files change or a certificate is about to expire.
  • STINOMENT bot on Telegram (optional, one click): urgent alerts at once (site down, fatal error, changed files, a new admin), a check every 5 minutes that the site is up, and one short report a week. Never more than a few urgent messages a day.
  • An activity log of logins and important changes.

Growth

  • Speed test of any page, like GTmetrix or PageSpeed: a grade from A to F, Core Web Vitals, screenshots of the page while it loads, the problems in plain words with a fix button for each one, and which plugin, theme or other site makes the page heavy. Real visitors next to the test, before and after, 6 months of real-visitor history and a weekly test that warns when the site gets slower.
  • Site strength and trust: domain strength from 0 to 10 (free Open PageRank data, the same idea as Domain Authority) and a trust score from 0 to 100 built from your own site (like a spam score, but you can fix each part), month by month since you started.
  • Weekly growth moves picked from your own data, with clear steps.
  • Competitor watch: speed, page size, structured data and new content of up to five competitors.
  • Your brand in AI answers: what an AI says about your brand from memory and after a web search, how many other sites write about you, and steps so AI tools recommend you.
  • Link opportunities: which sites link to your competitors, and which of them do not link to you yet. Data from the open Common Crawl web map, made about every 3 months. 7 linking sites per competitor for free, the full list with Premium.
  • Store money leaks for WooCommerce: failed payments, unpaid checkouts, best sellers out of stock.
  • Real visitor speed (Core Web Vitals from real visits, no cookies) with advice for every weak number.
  • Push notifications (off by default): visitors follow your site with one click on a bell; you see how many follow you and send them a message. Messages go straight from your site to the browsers’ push services.
  • Local business data, and a monthly report you can print or email.
  • Hints in the Posts, Pages and Products lists that show which items need attention.

Does the plugin send my data anywhere?

No personal data is sent. All checks run on your own server: the plugin requests your own pages, the links inside your posts (to see if they still work) and api.wordpress.org (to see when your plugins were last updated). Anything else goes only to services you turn on or open yourself (see “External services”). The STINOMENT Web Report is off by default. If you turn it on, only anonymous monthly totals are sent (search words only with a second, separate switch), you can read them first, and turning it off deletes them.

Does the plugin change my site by itself?

No. Checks only read your site. Changes happen when you click a fix button (or “Do it” on a change the AI assistant suggests), and each one can be undone from the “History & undo” tab. The only automatic housekeeping is removing the plugin’s own old backups after the number of days you set.

Are my backups deleted when I delete the plugin?

No. Backups are your data, so they stay in a hidden folder inside wp-content/uploads (its name starts with “stinoment-backups-“). You can download or delete them by FTP.

How do I get back in if I forget my private login address or lose my phone?

Add define( 'STSD_LOGIN_URL_OFF', true ); (private address) or define( 'STSD_2FA_OFF', true ); (two-step login) to wp-config.php with your host’s file manager. Another administrator can also turn two-step login off for you, and you have ten backup codes.

Why does “Sign in with Google” say “coming soon”?

This method needs a final review by Google. Until then, the “STINOMENT email” method gives you the same numbers and takes about two minutes. The Site Kit and own-key methods work as well.

Will it slow down my site?

No. Checks run in the admin area or in a daily background job, never when visitors open your pages.

Do I need an SEO plugin?

No. Growth Assistant checks titles and descriptions on its own and works with Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress and The SEO Framework if you use one. It only warns you when two SEO plugins run at the same time.

Can you help us with our site?

Yes. The “About us” screen in the plugin has a short form that reaches our team, or you can write to us through https://stinoment.com.

What does the STINOMENT Web Report send?

off by default; only if you turn on “Share anonymous monthly totals” in Growth → STINOMENT Web Report. Once a month a summary of the month before is sent: Google and Bing totals (clicks, views, position, device and country shares, click rate by position), the health score and which checks pass, real speed numbers, the trust score, domain strength and phone speed test score of the month (when you use those tools), the count of wrong password tries and spam comments, whether two-step login and a private login address are on, and the WordPress and PHP versions, language, number of posts, whether WooCommerce is active, and the month you started using the plugin. With the first summary only, the Google totals (clicks, views, position) of the two months before are also sent, so STINOMENT can measure how sites change after they start. It also includes kinds of searches without the words (questions or not, short or long, with or without your site name). Only if you also turn on “Also share popular search words”, your top Google searches are sent, after any search with an email, link, phone number or your site name is removed. In return, the site gets its own monthly report as a PDF file, sent by the STINOMENT server through the STINOMENT bot (if connected) and to the email the admin gives (optional). For that report only, the summary also carries the site name and address, the titles of pages whose Google clicks grew or dropped, what the plugin fixed that month, the three most useful tasks and that email; this part is never published, is used only to make and send the report, and is deleted when sharing is turned off. Visitor data, user names and passwords are never sent. You can read the exact summary on that screen before you agree. STINOMENT publishes only numbers that at least 10 sites share. Turning sharing off deletes everything your site shared. If you also turn on “List my site among STINOMENT users”, your site name and address may be shown as a STINOMENT user. Privacy policy: https://stinoment.com/privacy-policy/

What does the STINOMENT bot send?

only after you press “Connect” in Security → Alerts and press Start in the bot. Then your site address, site name, language, the address of your Growth Assistant screen and the plugin’s private health address are sent to the STINOMENT server. The server opens that health address about every 5 minutes to see if the site is up. The text of urgent alerts (fatal error, changed WordPress files, a new administrator or plugin, a certificate or domain about to end) and a short weekly report (health score, number of problems, the three most useful tasks, Google clicks of the week, blocked password tries, backup age) are sent to the server, which forwards them only to the people who connected the bot. Send /stop to the bot or press Disconnect to end it; deactivating the plugin disconnects it too. Privacy policy: https://stinoment.com/privacy-policy/ · Telegram: https://telegram.org/tos · https://telegram.org/privacy · Bale: https://bale.ai/

What does the AI assistant send?

when you open the Assistant screen, your site address and the site language are sent to the STINOMENT server to see your plan and your free AI action; nothing else. When you write a message in the Assistant chat or press an AI task button: Your message, the chat so far, and a short summary of your site made by the plugin’s own checks (site name and address, language, theme, numbers of posts and pages, health score, the problems found, and your Search Console totals and top search words if connected) are sent to the STINOMENT server, which passes them to Anthropic’s Claude API to write the answer. To do the job you ask for, the AI may also read parts of your site, and these parts are sent the same way: titles, short texts and categories of posts, pages and products; names and descriptions of categories and tags; comments (text, author name, author website, date; never email or IP addresses) when you ask about comments; the main WordPress settings when you ask about settings; the settings of this plugin, of other plugins or of the theme when you ask about them (secrets such as keys, passwords and licenses are always hidden and never sent); and the places where a text you name is found. The chat itself is kept on your own site for two days. Your rules for the AI and the facts in its memory (Rules and memory, above the chat) are kept on your site and sent with each AI question, unless you turn them off there. For a task, only the page or post it is about is sent (its address, title, description or text, and its search words). For the content coach, also your answers to its questions and the titles and addresses of up to ten related posts (for internal links); pictures and other parts are not sent. The answer comes back to your site; nothing changes until you press Apply. The server keeps only the cost and time of each request, not the text. Privacy policy: https://stinoment.com/privacy-policy/ · Anthropic: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms · https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy

1.4.2

  • New: the AI assistant reads and changes the settings of Growth Assistant, other plugins and the theme (secrets always hidden), adds CSS and safe HTML, clears the cache of common cache plugins, and reads competitors’ newest posts or any public page you name. Code it writes (PHP, JavaScript) is only shown for you to copy; the plugin never runs it.
  • New: Rules and memory. Write once what the AI must always follow (or add it from a text file), and let the AI learn your site: it saves short facts it can use in every chat. You can read, add and delete every fact.
  • New: the AI assistant now does the work. Ask in your own words and it reads your posts, pages, products, categories, tags, comments, settings and Elementor designs, then changes titles, descriptions, categories, tags, comments, footer and widget texts, Elementor texts and colors, and site settings. You see every change first and press “Do it”; every change can be undone. The AI never edits code or files and never deletes anything for ever.
  • New: example jobs under the chat, and a “New chat” button.
  • Also in this version (1.3.3 was not released):
  • New: Your brand in AI answers. Ask an AI what it really says about your brand, first from its own memory and then after a web search. See which other sites write about you, and get steps so AI tools like ChatGPT and Gemini recommend you (free sites once a week, Premium once a day).
  • New: try Premium free for a few days. Join the STINOMENT bot and start your free days from the Premium screen (one time per site, no payment).
  • New: turn off RSS feeds with one switch. Good for shops and company sites: feed links leave your pages, and every feed address goes to its normal page with a permanent redirect. The switch says if your site should keep its feeds (blogs, news sites, podcasts).
  • New: talk to the AI about a new version in the content coach. Write what you want changed (“shorter”, “add the delivery time”) and see the new version again before anything goes on your site (Premium).
  • New: ask the AI assistant for a new article. It plans the title, headings and a category, then writes the whole article as a draft, with a picture from your Media Library when one fits (Premium).
  • New: Link opportunities. See which sites link to your competitors, and which of them do not link to you yet (7 per competitor free, the full list with Premium).
  • New: plugin alerts in your browser can be turned on from Security → Alerts.
  • New: “Ask Google to index” in the Posts list and the editor opens Google’s check of that page in Search Console, where one click asks Google to read it again.
  • New: blog posts get Article data (title, dates, author, picture) for Google, only when no SEO plugin adds it already.
  • Better: the AI links in the Posts, Pages and Products lists are now one small “AI tools” menu.
  • Better: Google’s spam-policy check shows each page with links to open it on the site or in the editor.
  • Fix: the spam-policy check no longer flags normal words that contain a spam word (like “specialist”).
  • Fix: the competitor table showed 0 pages in your sitemap when your domain name contains the word “user”.
  • Fix: the chat no longer jumps while the answer is typed.
  • Fix: real visitor speed also counts visitors on Safari and in-app browsers.
  • Removed: the site health badge. A badge on a site can look like a trust seal, and we only check technical health.
  • Clearer: “Pages that no other page links to” explains that it counts links coming in, not links going out.

1.3.1

  • The whole 27-day growth plan is now shown to every site, free or Premium.
  • Search Console: each connection way links to its own step-by-step guide on stinoment.com.
  • Clearer plugin description and a clearer list of what the Assistant screen sends.

1.3.0

  • New: AI assistant. Ask questions about your own site in a chat; answers use what the plugin’s own checks found. Ready AI tasks: a better Google title and description for a page, and questions and answers (FAQ) for a post, each shown before anything changes and with Undo.
  • New: the free plan includes one AI action every 24 hours. The rest of the plugin stays completely free.
  • New: start an AI task from where you work: “Better title with AI” next to each page in Search Console, and “Better Google title (AI)” and “FAQ (AI)” under each post in the Posts list and in a small box in the editor.
  • New: monthly PDF report of your own site (fixes, Google clicks, pages that grew or dropped, comparison with similar sites), sent to the bot and by email, for sites that join the STINOMENT Web Report.
  • New: “Keep me posted” box on every screen: connect the STINOMENT bot or turn on browser alerts for urgent problems in one click.
  • New: 27-day growth plan: a week-by-week list built from your check-up (fixes tick themselves when done), with before and after numbers and a growth score.
  • New (Premium): “Social posts (AI)” under each post and product: ready posts for Instagram, X, LinkedIn and Telegram to copy. And “New article ideas” in the AI assistant: six ideas with a title and outline from your own Google search words, each with a “Write this post” button: it makes a draft, the AI asks you a few questions about your own experience, then writes the whole article with your answers for you to read before it goes into the draft. Nothing is published by the plugin.
  • New: Content coach (Growth). Every day it picks two weak posts or products on your own site (short text, no headings, no pictures, no links, not updated for a long time) and shows what is missing. With Premium, the AI asks you a few short questions, writes a clearer and fuller version with your answers, and shows it next to the old one. Nothing changes until you press “Put it on my site”, pictures and other parts stay as they are, and one click puts the old version back. Also “Improve with AI” under each post, page and product.
  • New (Premium): “Better title (AI)” for posts, pages and WooCommerce products. The AI reads the text and suggests three clear names that work for Google and for AI answers (SEO and GEO). You pick one; the address of the page does not change, and Undo puts the old name back.
  • New (Premium): “Check before publishing”, a kind editor’s check of a post, and “Refresh an old post”, which finds out-of-date parts and drafts new sections and a better title. Nothing changes until you press a button, and everything can be undone.
  • New: “Report a problem” link at the bottom of every screen.
  • New: a short, optional question when a Premium plan is not renewed.

1.2.0

  • New: Premium screen. See the plan, prices and what the AI features do; pay with USDT (TRON) or Bitcoin with a QR code; the plan turns on by itself when the payment is confirmed; official invoices. Opens for sales together with the AI features.
  • New: safety lock – the payment screen only ever shows STINOMENT wallets built into the plugin.

1.1.0

  • New: make old images lighter by section (blog, shop, Media Library) at the quality you pick, after seeing a real before/after sample. Clear advice on how low is too low, and undo for every run.
  • New: PNG uploads and old PNG images can become WebP too (see-through parts stay see-through).
  • New check: Google penalty risk. Finds spam topics, hidden links, keyword stuffing, paid links without rel=”sponsored”, link farms, scaled content and doorway pages, and names the Google system each one touches, in plain words.
  • New check: author profiles (E-E-A-T). Writers without a real name, bio, link or photo are listed with what is missing.
  • New check: your brand name and main searches on Google, from your Search Console data, with praise when it goes well and clear next steps when it does not.
  • New: the Posts, Pages and Products lists show if each post is growing or falling on Google against the 28 days before, from saved data only.
  • New: Search Console in one plain sentence on the overview, in the weekly email and in the Telegram report.
  • New: domain and SSL countdown on the overview. Domain reminders start one month before the end and come every week (every day in the last week). .ir domains are read from IRNIC.
  • New: add or remove sitemaps in Search Console when you connect with your own Google key.
  • New: AI assistants can use every Toolbox tool and read the history through the WordPress Abilities API.
  • Fixed: valid structured data is no longer reported as broken; fixed broken links leave the list at once; missing pages count people and search engines apart and no longer count other robots.
  • Questions are asked inside the page instead of browser pop-ups, so the screen never freezes (and AI assistants and test tools can press the buttons).
  • The menu now sits right under Dashboard.
  • Fixed: after an update, sites whose speed plugin removes “?ver=” from file addresses (with Cloudflare in front) kept showing the old screen.

1.0.4

  • More accurate: “as Google sees it” now shows the exact address, answer code and time it tested, skips pages that answer “not found”, ignores lazy-load placeholders, and checks big claims (no H1, no canonical) a second time before reporting them.
  • Every card shows when it was checked, with “Check this again” and “Copy link”. Counts say what they count, and plugin and update numbers refresh at once.
  • One click writes alt text for every image with a good guess (images without a good guess are left alone), and turns extra H1s into H2 in all posts.
  • Products that are sold out are no longer reported as “missing a price”; free products are fine too.
  • New: “Can ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity find you?” checks AI search and training robots in robots.txt, with two safe settings.
  • New: SEO tags printed twice (title, canonical, description, structured data), with the probable source of each copy.
  • New: hide thin tag pages from Google without an SEO plugin; missing pages grouped by kind, with standard redirects per kind.
  • New: test email in one click and a DKIM check. Old sitemaps still submitted in Search Console, and sitemaps that show login names, are found.
  • New Advanced tab: technical checks, and how to let an AI assistant work with the plugin (WordPress Abilities API), with a preview ability. Copy the report or download it as JSON.
  • Weekly moves show about how long each takes and how big the effect is. Better labels for screen readers.

1.0.3

  • Fixed: downloading a large full backup could fail with “invalid response” or a fatal error on hosts with output buffering. Downloads now stream in pieces and can resume.
  • Fatal error alerts now say which plugin or theme and the error line.
  • Search Console: choose 7 days, 28 days, 3, 6, 12 or 16 months. New cards for Google Images, Video, News, Discover and special result types.
  • Search Console: sitemap warnings explained, with a check that finds the cause. The deprecated “indexed” number is gone.
  • New: links from other sites (from Bing), with lost links and a one-click redirect.
  • New: “Don’t remind me” for any finding, and for single parts (products without a price, image or description; posts in the default category; empty categories). Turn them on again in Settings.
  • Smarter: a renamed default category is treated as a real topic. Alt text is never guessed from machine file names (hashes, IMG_1234).
  • HTTPS: when the certificate already works, one click moves the site to https (undo in History), with a new “Send every visitor to https” switch. Without a certificate, the steps for cPanel, DirectAdmin or Plesk.
  • New: cookie consent banner with real blocking and Consent Mode v2.
  • Privacy: suggested text for Settings, Privacy.

1.0.2

  • New checks: trust pages (privacy policy, terms, contact, about, returns), phone-friendly layout, and posts with the same text.
  • New: Push notifications (off by default) with follower count and messages.
  • New: STINOMENT bot on Telegram or Bale, connected with one click: urgent alerts, uptime checks every 5 minutes and a weekly report.
  • Backups: a backup counts for 30 days even after you download and delete the file, and you get one reminder a month when it is time for a new one.
  • A finding solved with a tool leaves the list at once, without waiting for the next check-up.
  • Findings that usually need a specialist now say that the STINOMENT team can help.
  • New: Speed test like GTmetrix and PageSpeed, with which plugin makes the page heavy, a fix for each problem, before and after, 6 months of real-visitor history and a weekly test.
  • New: Site strength and trust: domain strength (0-10) and a trust score (0-100), month by month.
  • New checks: structured data (schema), security headers, links and buttons without a name.
  • New switch: Always use https (HSTS).

1.0.1

  • Review fixes: safer JSON-LD output, no inline styles, lower menu position, two-step login reminder is now opt-in, rollback copies of plugins removed, external services documented.

1.0.0

  • First public release.

short_description: A free daily check-up for your site: Google numbers in plain words, security, backups, image tools and AI help. One click to fix, one click to undo.
description:
Is your site slow, hard to find on Google, or not safe? Most owners find out too late, when the visitors are already gone.

Growth Assistant checks your whole site every day. Then it tells you, in plain words, what is wrong, where it is, why it matters and how to fix it. Many problems have a fix button. Nothing changes until you click it, and you can undo every change.

The plugin is free. You do not need an account or a subscription. It is made by STINOMENT, a team that has helped hundreds of websites grow. We use it every day on our own sites and on our clients’ sites.

1. A daily check-up with more than 50 checks

Security, site health, SEO, content, links, speed, WooCommerce and comments. Every finding comes with clear next steps. Each day you also see the three tasks that help your site the most.

2. Google and Bing numbers you can understand

Connect Google Search Console (four easy ways) and Bing. You see clicks, views and position for up to 16 months. The plugin also tells you which pages are close to page one, which pages are losing visitors, and why Google has a problem with your sitemap.

3. Image tools: alt text, smaller files and WebP

  • Writes alt text for all your images in one click. The text comes from the page where the image is used, so Google understands your pictures.
  • Makes big images much lighter. You see a real before and after sample first.
  • Changes JPG and PNG images to WebP, the modern format. Your old files are kept, so you can undo at any time.

4. Security that does not get in your way

  • Login protection, a private login address and two-step login.
  • File health: your files are compared with the real files from WordPress.org.
  • Alerts by email, Telegram or webhook when the site goes down or a file changes.
  • An activity log of logins and important changes.

5. Backups

A content backup or a full backup of all files, made in small steps so it works on shared hosting. You choose how many days to keep them.

6. Speed test

Test any page on phone or computer. You get a grade from A to F, the problems in plain words, a fix for each one, and the plugin or theme that makes the page heavy.

7. Tools to grow

  • A 27-day growth plan built from your own check-up, week by week.
  • A content coach that finds your weak posts and products each day and shows what is missing.
  • Site strength and trust scores, month by month.
  • Competitor watch, store money leaks for WooCommerce, push notifications and a monthly report.

8. A toolbox for everyday work

Redirects for missing pages, safe editing of robots.txt, llms.txt and .htaccess, email delivery (SMTP), a cookie banner that really waits for consent, protection switches and more.

9. An AI assistant that does the work for you

Tell the AI what you want, in your own words: “find the posts about fake pages and change their titles”, “move Russian spam comments with links to spam”, “write descriptions for my top tags”, “change the copyright text in my footer”, “change this Elementor button”, “are my settings standard?”. It reads your site, then shows a card with every change. Nothing changes until you press “Do it”, and every change can be undone. It also manages plugin and theme settings, CSS and the cache, and reads competitors’ posts. It never runs code (code it writes is only shown to copy), never touches users or passwords, and never deletes anything for ever. Give it your own rules once (text or a file), and it keeps a memory of your site, so every answer fits your business. Free sites get one AI question every 24 hours.

Want more help from AI?

Premium gives you more AI each day, plus social posts, article ideas and full drafts written with your own answers, and a refresh for old posts. All checks and tools above stay free for everyone.

Built for everyday hosting

Work runs in short steps or small background jobs, never while visitors open your pages. English and Persian, with “?” notes on every screen.

Works with AI assistants

On WordPress 6.9+, the report, fixes, undo and Toolbox tools are in the Abilities API for MCP assistants (administrators only).

About STINOMENT

STINOMENT is an IT team that builds, fixes and grows websites, and can do the SEO and speed work for you.

  • English website, guides and plugin news: https://stinoment.com/
  • Persian website (فارسی): https://stinoment.com/fa/

External services

This plugin can connect to these services. Nothing personal is sent.

  • IndexNow (api.indexnow.org) – only when you turn on the IndexNow switch. When a post is published or updated, its address, your site host name and your IndexNow key are sent, so search engines that use IndexNow (Bing, Yandex and others) learn about the change. Documentation: https://www.indexnow.org/documentation · Microsoft privacy statement: https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement · Yandex legal documents: https://yandex.com/legal/
  • WordPress.org Plugins API (api.wordpress.org) – during a check-up, the folder names of your active plugins are sent to learn when each plugin was last updated. Privacy policy: https://wordpress.org/about/privacy/
  • WordPress.org files (api.wordpress.org, downloads.wordpress.org, core.svn.wordpress.org) – only when you use File health: your WordPress version and locale, and the folder name and version of each plugin, are sent to download the original file fingerprints; to repair a WordPress file, that original file is downloaded. Privacy policy: https://wordpress.org/about/privacy/
  • Google Search Console API (searchconsole.googleapis.com, oauth2.googleapis.com) – only with the “own key” Search Console method: your site’s property address and the date ranges are sent with your own service account, to read your search numbers. When you press “Add to Search Console” or “Remove from Search Console” on the Search tab, the sitemap address is also sent, to add it to or remove it from your property. Terms: https://developers.google.com/terms · Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • STINOMENT server (api.stinoment.com) – only with the “STINOMENT email” or “Sign in with Google” methods: your site address and a random check token are sent once to register the site, then the property and date ranges of each Search Console request. The server reads Google’s numbers for you and returns them; it does not keep them. Privacy policy: https://stinoment.com/privacy-policy/
  • STINOMENT contact form (api.stinoment.com) – only when you fill in the form on the “About us” screen, tick the agreement box and press “Send message”: your name, email, phone (if given), website address, the service you chose and your message are sent so the STINOMENT team can answer you. Nothing is sent before that. Privacy policy: https://stinoment.com/privacy-policy/
  • STINOMENT Web Report (api.stinoment.com) – off by default; only if you turn on “Share anonymous monthly totals” in Growth → STINOMENT Web Report. Once a month, anonymous totals of the month before are sent (search, health, speed and security numbers, no visitor data, no user names, no passwords). You can read the exact summary before you agree, and turning it off deletes everything your site shared. The full list is in the FAQ: “What does the STINOMENT Web Report send?”. Privacy policy: https://stinoment.com/privacy-policy/
  • Browser push services – only if you turn on Push notifications and press “Send”, or an admin turns on “Browser alerts” in the “Keep me posted” box (then only when something urgent happens on the site). For each follower the site sends an empty, signed request to the push address their own browser gave (Google Firebase Cloud Messaging for Chrome, Edge on Android and Opera; Mozilla for Firefox; Microsoft for Edge on Windows; Apple for Safari). The message text is not sent to them: the visitor’s browser then reads it from your own site. The push addresses are kept only in your database and are deleted with the plugin. Google: https://firebase.google.com/terms · https://policies.google.com/privacy · Mozilla: https://www.mozilla.org/about/legal/terms/services/ · https://www.mozilla.org/privacy/ · Microsoft: https://www.microsoft.com/servicesagreement · https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement · Apple: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/terms/site.html · https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/
  • STINOMENT bot (api.stinoment.com, with Telegram api.telegram.org or Bale tapi.bale.ai) – only after you press “Connect” in Security → Alerts and press Start in the bot. Your site address and name, the alert text and a short weekly report are sent, and the server checks about every 5 minutes that your site is up. Full list in the FAQ: “What does the STINOMENT bot send?”. Privacy policy: https://stinoment.com/privacy-policy/ · Telegram: https://telegram.org/tos · https://telegram.org/privacy · Bale: https://bale.ai/
  • Speed test (api.stinoment.com, with Google PageSpeed Insights and Chrome UX Report) – only when you press “Test on phone” or “Test on computer” in Growth → Speed test, and then once a week if you keep the weekly test on. The address of the page you test (a page of your own site), the device and your language are sent to the STINOMENT server, which asks Google’s PageSpeed Insights to open the page and sends back the scores, the problems and small screenshots. Pressing “Show the 6 months” sends your site address to read Google’s public real-visitor numbers (Chrome UX Report). No visitor data is sent. Privacy policy: https://stinoment.com/privacy-policy/ · Google terms: https://developers.google.com/terms · Google privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • Site strength (api.stinoment.com, with Open PageRank by DomCop) – only after you press “Check domain strength” in Growth → Site strength and trust, then once a month. Only your domain name is sent; the STINOMENT server asks Open PageRank for its public score and rank. The trust score is worked out on your own site and nothing is sent for it. Privacy policy: https://stinoment.com/privacy-policy/ · Open PageRank service and terms: https://www.domcop.com/openpagerank/
  • Google Site Kit – with the Site Kit method, data is read from the Site Kit plugin inside your own site; Site Kit talks to Google under its own terms.
  • Bing Webmaster Tools API (ssl.bing.com) – only after you add a Bing API key: your site address and key are sent to read your Bing numbers, and the addresses of your most linked pages to read who links to them. Microsoft privacy statement: https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement
  • Telegram Bot API (api.telegram.org) and Bale Bot API (tapi.bale.ai) – only if you add a bot token: the alert text (site name, what happened, your site address) is sent to the chat you choose. Telegram terms: https://telegram.org/tos · privacy: https://telegram.org/privacy · Bale: https://bale.ai/
  • Your own webhook (Slack, Discord, Google Chat, Teams) – only if you add one: the same alert text is sent to that address.
  • IRNIC WHOIS (whois.nic.ir, port 43) – only for sites on a .ir domain, because .ir domains are not in RDAP. Once a week the site’s domain name is sent to read when the registration ends. Nothing else is sent. Service by IRNIC, the .ir registry. Terms and privacy: https://www.nic.ir/
  • STINOMENT Premium (api.stinoment.com) – only when you open the Premium screen. Sent: your site address, the admin’s IP address and the site language, to show the price and check that the AI is offered in your region (the IP is stored only when refused). When you buy: the email you type and the transaction ID you paste. “Start my free days” sends the same details, and the server checks the bot link (and the Web Report when asked). Payment goes from your own wallet to STINOMENT; the plugin never sees wallet keys. Terms: https://stinoment.com/terms/ Privacy: https://stinoment.com/privacy-policy/
  • STINOMENT AI assistant (api.stinoment.com, with Anthropic’s Claude API) – when you open the Assistant screen, write a message or press an AI task button. Sent: your message, the chat, a short site summary, and the parts of your site the AI reads for your job (full list in the FAQ: “What does the AI assistant send?”). The server passes them to Anthropic and keeps only the cost and time, not the text. Privacy: https://stinoment.com/privacy-policy/ · Anthropic: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy
  • STINOMENT problem report (api.stinoment.com) – only when you fill in “Report a problem” and press Send: your text, your email (if given), your site address and the WordPress, PHP and plugin versions are sent so the STINOMENT team can fix it.
  • RDAP service (rdap.org) – only if you turn on the domain expiry alert. Once a week your site’s domain name (for example example.com) is sent to read when the domain registration ends. Nothing else is sent. Service by the RDAP.org project, which forwards the request to the registry of your domain: https://about.rdap.org/ · Privacy information: https://about.rdap.org/#privacy
  • STINOMENT brand check (api.stinoment.com, with Anthropic’s Claude API and web search) – only when you press “Ask the AI” in Growth → Your brand in AI answers. Sent: your brand name, site address and screen language. The server keeps only the cost, time and date of your last check; the answer is kept on your site. Privacy: https://stinoment.com/privacy-policy/ · Anthropic: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy
  • STINOMENT link data (api.stinoment.com) – only when you open Growth → Link opportunities. Domain names only are sent: your own domain and the competitor domains on that screen. The server answers from the open Common Crawl web graph (https://commoncrawl.org/terms-of-use) and deletes its own copy of the answers after about 10 days; your answers are kept on your site. Privacy policy: https://stinoment.com/privacy-policy/
  • Competitor sites and pages you ask about – Competitor watch opens the sites you add at most once a day (home page, sitemap, feed). In the AI assistant, when you ask, it opens the feed or public WordPress API of competitors you name, or a public page you name, like a visitor; the text goes to the AI to answer you.
  • Websites you link to (link checker) – during the broken links check, the plugin opens the addresses that appear in your own posts, with a plain request that sends no personal data, to see if the page still exists. Each site is a different service under its own terms.
  • YouTube thumbnails (i.ytimg.com) – only if you turn on the lightweight video embeds switch. Visitors’ browsers load the video’s preview picture from YouTube, and YouTube’s player loads only after a click. Terms: https://www.youtube.com/t/terms · Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Included libraries

  • QR Code Generator for JavaScript by Kazuhiko Arase, MIT license (assets/js/vendor/qrcode.js), used to show the two-step login QR code.
  • Fonts under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 (assets/fonts, license files next to them): Vazirmatn by Saber Rastikerdar, Lalezar by Borna Izadpanah, Inter by Rasmus Andersson. Used in the admin screens and the cookie banner, loaded from your own site.

The “STINOMENT” and “Stinoment Growth Assistant” names, brands and logos belong to STINOMENT. Publishing any copy or modified version of this plugin under the STINOMENT name or brand without written permission is prohibited.
